“The Cost of Flexibility: Informal Governance and Resilience in the Minibus Taxi Industry in South Africa.”
Christopher F. Eaglin and Rakeen Tanvir. Revise and resubmit at the Strategic Management Journal, 2026.
We study how the management of informal institutions shapes small-firm performance in South Africa’s minibus taxi industry. Using administrative loan records, high-frequency GPS data, and weather shocks, we find that organizational flexibility increases vehicle utilization and improves loan repayment, though it does not fully protect firms when severe shocks occur.

title: Rakeen Tanvir
text:
Research
I study strategy—how firms’ choices shape their outcomes—with a focus on:

Science and innovation: how firms create and use new ideas
Entrepreneurship: startups, small firms, and their founders
Labor automation: how AI and new technology change work

With Christopher F. Eaglin, I study informal governance and resilience in the South African taxi industry. In separate work with Manuel González-Astudillo (Federal Reserve Board of Governors), I study how the Federal Reserve’s “dot plot” can be used to infer intended monetary policy responses to inflation and economic activity.
More broadly, my interests span strategic management, innovation and entrepreneurship, economic history, science and technology, and the economics of AI and automation.

Background
Before starting my PhD, I was a Research Assistant in Macroeconomics & Quantitative Studies at the Federal Reserve Board of Governors, and earlier spent several years in industry, including at MathWorks. I hold a B.A. in Psychology from Boston College.
